reason: The hypothesis relies on a solute-drag mechanism in FeNiCrMn, but the cited evidence (E1–E3) concerns different alloys (Al0.7CoCrFeNi, NiCrFeCoMn) and phonon drag, not solute drag. No cited passage provides specific prior evidence for solute/dislocation drag in Co-free FeNiCrMn, nor for the claimed effect of heat treatments on dislocation density and solute atmospheres in this system. The cited evidence is therefore misrepresented or only loosely related to the key premises.
premises: Dynamic strength–ductility in FeNiCrMn is governed by rate-dependent dislocation drag from solute/dislocation interactions.
Post-casting heat treatments can modulate dislocation density and solute atmospheres to control activation energy for glide.
At high strain rates, enhanced solute drag elevates yield strength and sustains ductility via work hardening.
Phonon or solute drag effects become dominant at high dislocation velocities under dynamic loading.
Dislocation density and solute distribution can be systematically varied by subcritical annealing.
